masterclasses.title: Kidney - Anatomy Lecture

summary_preview.content: • Vertebral Extent: T12 to L3; Right Kidney is -1.5 cm lower due to right hepatic lobe. • Dimensions: 12 × 6 × 3 cm. Average weight: 150 g in males, 135 g in females. • Hilum: Vertical slit at medial border opposite L1 (Transpyloric plane).

• Hilum Order (Ant to Post): Vein -> Artery - Pelvis (V-A-P). • 4 Protective Layers: (1) Fibrous capsule (strips easily in health), (2) Perirenal fat, (3) Gerota's renal fascia (splits into anterior Toldt & posterior Zuckerkandl), (4) Pararenal fat. • Critical Point: Gerota's fascia remains open INFERIORLY -> allows extravasated pus/urine/blood to track into pelvis.

masterclasses.title: Anatomy of Urethra (Male & Female) - Anatomy Tutorial

summary_preview.content: - Narrowest Points: External urethral meatus is narrowest overall (rigid); membranous urethra is narrowest and least dilatable inside. • Widest Points: Prostatic urethra (most dilatable) and Fossa Navicularis in glans penis. • Posterior Wall Features: Urethral crest -> expands into Colliculus Seminalis (Verumontanum). • Prostatic Utricle: Blind cul-de-sac at center of verumontanum; homologue of female Uterus and Vagina. • Ejaculatory Ducts: Open on either side of the prostatic utricle. • Prostatic Sinuses: Grooves on sides of crest receiving 15-20 ducts of the prostatic gland. • BPH vs Cancer: BPH affects periurethral Transition Zone (early obstruction); Cancer affects Peripheral Zone (posterior, no early obstruction). • Membranous Urethra: Traverses Deep Perineal Pouch; surrounded by striated External Urethral Sphincter (Pudendal nerve S2-S4).
• Cowper's (Bulbourethral) Glands: Lie in deep perineal pouch; ducts pierce perineal membrane to open into bulbous spongy urethra.

masterclasses.title: Development of the Urinary System - Embryology Lecture

summary_preview.content: Anorectal Canal (dorsally). • Perineal Body: Fusion site of urorectal septum with cloacal membrane; splits membrane into Urogenital & Anal membranes. • Vesical Part (Cranial): Forms Body & Apex of Urinary Bladder; continuous with allantois / urachus. • Pelvic Part (Middle): Forms lower prostatic & membranous urethra in males; entire urethra (4 cm) in females. • Phallic Part (Caudal): Forms spongy urethra (shaft) in males; vestibule of vagina in females. • Navicular Fossa: Formed by ectodermal ingrowth from the glans penis tip (canalization).

masterclasses.title: General Structure of the Kidney - Histology Lecture

summary_preview.content: • Capsule: Dense irregular collagenous CT with contractile myofibroblasts. • Cortical Interstitial Cells: Fibroblast-like cells produce Erythropoietin (EPO) in hypoxia. • Medullary Interstitial Cells: Lipid-laden interstitial cells synthesize PGE2 and Medullipin I (vasodepressor lipid). • Cortex (Granular): Renal corpuscles, PCTs, DCTs, and cortical labyrinths.

• Medullary Rays (Ferrein): Parallel straight tubules (loops of Henle) & collecting ducts radiating from medullary base. • Renal Lobe: 1 pyramid + overlying cortex + 1/2 adjacent Bertin columns (~8-18 per kidney). • Renal Lobule: Central medullary ray + surrounding cortical labyrinths, delimited laterally by Interlobular Arteries. • Nephron Composition: Corpuscle, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT. (Collecting ducts are NOT part of nephron proper).
